references.text: Another Levite from Bethlehem in Judah who was also traveling, which shows a pattern of Levites wandering at this time.
The Levite again mentions Bethlehem in Judah as his hometown, the same place of origin as the Levite in Judges 17:9.
Bethlehem in Judah is mentioned as the home of Elimelech and Naomi, the same city from which the Levite came.
Bethlehem in Judah is mentioned as David's hometown, the same place from which the Levite came.
The Levites were not given their own territory and depended on cities that were assigned to them, which explains why this Levite had to wander to find a place to live.
The Israelites were reminded to take care of the Levites since they had no inheritance, providing background for the Levite's situation.
The law allowed Levites to move from one place to another and serve at the sanctuary, which explains the Levite's wandering.
